requirements.title: External-file access methods are sequential, direct, and stream
requirements.definition: There are three methods of accessing external-file data: sequential, direct, and stream.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

Access-position fixture implementation: 1 valid run-phase scratch-file program(s) cover `direct-access-method`, `sequential-access-method`, `stream-access-method`. They create the external files in the run directory with STATUS='SCRATCH' and also close with STATUS='DELETE'. Oracles are limited to exact integer/character values, character lengths, IOSTAT zero, IOSTAT_END, and POS= inequalities or values fixed by this source. No file name, external representation, processor-specific IOSTAT number, IOMSG text, formatted-stream byte spacing, or unsupported cross-access-method property is asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Runtime fixture coverage is finite and does not imply fixture review. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.

requirements.title: Allowed access methods can vary by file and processor
requirements.definition: Some files may allow more than one access method and other files may be restricted to one access method.

pending.multiple-access-methods-permitted: No portable oracle may require a file to support multiple methods; future tests must guard any cross-method behavior with processor support.
pending.single-access-method-restriction-permitt: No portable oracle may fail a processor merely because a particular file is restricted to one access method.

requirements.title: A file access method is determined at connection or preconnected-file creation
requirements.definition: The method of accessing a file is determined when the file is connected to a unit or when the file is created if it is preconnected.

pending.preconnected-access-method-determined-at: No portable oracle exists without a processor-described preconnected file; future tests must record the preconnected method through INQUIRE where available.
